title: Staggered Health Policy Adoption: Spillover Effects and Their Implications
authors: Vadim Elenev; Luis Quintero; Alessandro Rebucci; Emilia Simeonova
eligible_reason: Contiguous-county triplet design, not a unit-by-calendar-time TWFE. Each triplet (treated, neighbor, hinterland county) is an 8-day window (t = -4..3) around the treated county's stay-at-home order; counties recur across triplets (stacked event windows). Regressions use county FE plus an event-time Post dummy (no calendar-date FE), time-varying weather controls (temp, precipitation, snowfall) in every column, and two treatment regressors (Post x Treated direct effect and Post x Neighbor spillover). Event study uses event-time dummies interacted with relationship, again without calendar FE. Shipped data are synthetic (noise injected).
design_notes: run_all_regressions.py: main_spec = 'post + post:C(relationship) + temp + precipitation + snowfall' with '| county' FE (line 22, 137), weights='pair_pop' (triplet population), cluster = treated-county NPI date x treated-county state (master.ipynb cell 27 default). Outcomes: log_NonMed_visits_by_day, log_Rest_visits_by_day, log_Ret_visits_by_day, hrs_home, fracboth, frac_home (Table 2); DMA splits (Table 3). Triplets built in construct_contiguous_triplets.py (min 4-day adoption gap; hinterland must not adopt or border an adopter within 4 days) and expanded to t in [-4,3] with post = 1[t>=0] (expand_triplets, lines 112-118). Event study (run_eventstudy lines 305-343): C(t, Treatment(-1)) + C(t):C(relationship) + weather | county, Figure 4 / Table A.3. Table 4 (Stata do-file lines 149-152): reghdfe y ib1.relationshipn##post temp precipitation snowfall [pw=triplet_pop], absorb(origin_county) vce(cluster cluster) on directional traffic outcomes. Estimation via linearmodels AbsorbingLS wrapper (feols.py).
estimators_reported: Triplet (treated/neighbor/hinterland) DiD with county FE and event-time Post dummies, weighted, clustered (Python linearmodels)
Event-time event study within triplets (Figure 4, Table A.3)

software_detail: Python (pandas, linearmodels AbsorbingLS via custom feols wrapper, statsmodels; master.ipynb) plus Stata 17 (reghdfe, estout) for Table 4 and Figure A.2
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Design is explicitly built to avoid staggered-TWFE comparisons (Goodman-Bacon cited): each triplet contributes an 8-day window around the treated county's SHO date. Not convertible to an eligible spec without changing the design (would need county x calendar-date panel with date FE and no weather controls). SafeGraph data are proprietary; shipped files have noise injected (synthetic.py), seed withheld.
